newsitem.title: FRANCE: French construction industry to suffer from cold.
newsitem.headline: French construction industry to suffer from cold.

text.p: The cold snap which descended on France last week will have a "very strong" adverse impact on construction and public works companies, Alain Sionneau, president of the National Building Federation (FNB), said on Friday.

"In an average year about two weeks are lost due to bad weather. However, this year, the cold started earlier. If the winter is similar to January and February 1996, we risk having at least three weeks out in 1997," he told Reuters.
He said the economic consequences of bad weather affected the industry's entire production chain and weighed on all companies whatever their size.
The impact was relatively small during the week between Christmas and the New Year because construction and public works companies are traditionally closed.

But "the impact is going to be very strong now, since companies resumed work yesterday or will start again by Monday at the latest, and if I believe the weather forecast things are not going to improve quickly," Sionneau said.

"Masonry companies will be the worst affected. They are the first to be affected but the whole production chain will be hit. If the mason can't work today, that implies that in three months the plumber or the electrician will suffer a delay in work."

In December, the FNB predicted that turnover in the construction industry would decline 1.8 percent in 1997 after a drop of 2.6 percent in 1996 and that some 30,000 jobs would be lost compared with 40,000 last year.
